summary: Most requested features are present: backend profile model extended with optional health fields plus migration; frontend profile setup collects and saves those fields; dashboard adds a MaintenanceCaloriesCard and a hook to fetch computed health metrics; branding updated to “Calorieshivam” across web and Android wrapper. The main gap is REQ-37’s requirement that the health-metrics query return a structured “missing inputs” response instead of trapping—current backend logic appears to trap on missing fields, and the frontend hook anticipates traps.

missing_requirements.requirement: Backend health-metrics query should return a structured response indicating which required profile inputs are missing (and must not trap) when profile data is incomplete.
missing_requirements.reason: The new backend API `getCallerHealthMetrics` and its helper appear to call `Runtime.trap` when the profile is missing or individual fields are missing (e.g., missing height/weight). This violates the acceptance criterion requiring a structured, non-trapping response for missing inputs. The frontend hook also contains a comment indicating the backend will trap, suggesting no structured missing-field response was implemented.
